The theory of sexual selection is a concept in evolutionary biology that explains the development of traits that are advantageous in attracting mates, rather than in survival. These traits can be physical, such as colorful plumage in birds, or behavioral, such as singing in songbirds. Sexual selection can lead to the evolution of traits that are not directly related to survival, such as the elaborate courtship rituals seen in many species.
